questions.topic: Analytical Chemistry — identifying Fe3+ with NH4OH
concepts: Fe3+ gives reddish-brown ppt with NH4OH
questions.question: Ravi was asked to identify the cation present in the salt solution. He added one of the reagents given below and got a reddish-brown precipitate. The reagent that he used is:
questions.solution: (c) Ammonium hydroxide. NH4OH precipitates Fe3+ ions as reddish-brown ferric hydroxide: FeCl3 + 3NH4OH -> Fe(OH)3 + 3NH4Cl. The other reagents test anions (AgNO3, BaCl2) or give white precipitates.

questions.topic: Study of Compounds — action of dilute HCl on metals
concepts: metals above hydrogen displace H2 from acids
questions.question: Which metal does not react with HCl to form a colourless, odourless gas which burns with a pop sound?
questions.solution: (c) Cu. Copper is below hydrogen in the activity series, so it cannot displace hydrogen from dilute HCl; Ca, Mg and Zn all liberate H2 (burns with a pop).

questions.topic: Study of Compounds — ammonia from magnesium nitride
questions.question: Prateek added warm water to magnesium nitride, and a colourless gas evolved, which, when tested with phenolphthalein, turned it pink. The gas evolved is:
questions.solution: (b) Ammonia. Mg3N2 + 6H2O -> 3Mg(OH)2 + 2NH3. Ammonia is alkaline in water and turns phenolphthalein pink.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry — properties of ethane
concepts: alkanes are saturated with C-C single bonds
questions.question: Which of the following statements about ethane is false?

options.c: It is a gas at ordinary temperatures.
options.d: It has a triple bond between the carbon atoms.

questions.solution: (d) It has a triple bond between the carbon atoms. Ethane (CH3-CH3) is a saturated alkane with only a C-C single bond; it is a gas and undergoes substitution.

questions.topic: Metallurgy — thermite reaction
questions.question: Thermite mixture is used to weld the broken ends of the iron girders. This mixture consists of ferric oxide and aluminium powder, which, when heated, produces molten iron. In this reaction, the aluminium powder acts as a/an _________ agent.
questions.solution: (b) reducing. Fe2O3 + 2Al -> Al2O3 + 2Fe; aluminium removes oxygen from ferric oxide, so it acts as the reducing agent.

questions.topic: Electrolysis — anode reaction in electrolysis of acidulated water
questions.question: The diagram represents the electrolysis of acidulated water (Hofmann voltameter with platinum foil electrodes; oxygen collects over the anode and hydrogen over the cathode). The reaction occurring at the anode is:
questions.solution: (d) OH- - e- -> OH; 4OH -> 2H2O + O2. Hydroxyl ions migrate to the anode, lose electrons and the OH radicals combine to give water and oxygen.
questions.figure_desc: Hofmann voltameter for electrolysis of acidulated water with platinum foil anode and cathode; oxygen collected at anode, hydrogen at cathode.

questions.topic: Periodic Properties and Variations of Properties — atomic size in groups and periods
concepts: atomic size increases down a group and decreases across a period
questions.question:
A portion of the periodic table is given (letters are not actual symbols):
Groups:   1 | 2 | 13 | 14 | 15 | 16 | 17 | 18
Period 2: Li | - | D | - | - | O | J | Ne
Period 3: A | Mg | E | Si | - | H | K | -
Period 4: B | C | - | F | G | - | - | L
With reference to the portion of the periodic table given above, identify the element having the largest atomic size:
questions.solution: (b) B. B is in Group 1 (alkali metals) and Period 4. Atomic size increases down a group and decreases across a period, so the Group 1 element of the lowest period shown is the largest.

questions.topic: Electrolysis — electrolysis of lead bromide needs molten state
concepts: ionic solids conduct only when molten
ions not free in solid state
questions.question: The picture shows an apparatus that a teacher used for demonstrating the properties of ionic substances. The teacher heats a sample of lead bromide in a crucible which contains two electrodes which are part of the circuit shown (DC supply and a bulb). The bulb does not light up. What is the best explanation for this?

options.b: Molten lead bromide does not conduct electricity.
options.c: The sample of lead bromide was not heated up to the melting point by the teacher.
options.d: The DC power supply was set up correctly.

questions.solution: (c) The sample of lead bromide was not heated up to the melting point by the teacher. Solid PbBr2 has ions held in a fixed lattice, so it cannot conduct; only molten PbBr2 conducts (and the bulb would glow).
questions.figure_desc: Crucible of white lead bromide on a tripod over a burner with two electrodes connected through a bulb to a DC power supply.

questions.topic: Periodic Properties and Variations of Properties — cation formation by Group 2 element
concepts: metals lose electrons to form cations
questions.question: Element Y is in Group IIA of the Periodic Table. Y reacts with element Q to form an ionic compound. Which equation shows the process that takes place when Y forms ions?
questions.solution: (d) Y - 2e- -> Y2+. A Group 2 metal has 2 valence electrons and loses both to form a dipositive cation.

questions.topic: Electrolysis — movement of ions and electrons in silver plating
concepts: electrons flow from anode to positive terminal in external circuit
questions.question:
The diagram shows a circuit used to electrolyse aqueous sodium argento cyanide with silver electrodes. Arrow 1 points up the wire from the anode (+) towards the positive terminal of the power supply; arrow 2 points down the wire from the negative terminal towards the cathode (-); arrow 3 in the electrolyte points from the cathode towards the anode; arrow 4 in the electrolyte points from the anode towards the cathode.
Which arrow indicates the movement of the silver ions in the electrolyte and of the electrons in the external circuit?
questions.solution: (d) Silver ions: 4, Electrons: 1. Ag+ cations migrate through the electrolyte towards the cathode (arrow 4). Electrons released at the anode travel through the external wire to the positive terminal of the supply (arrow 1).
questions.figure_desc: Electrolytic cell with two silver electrodes in aqueous sodium argento cyanide; arrows 1 and 2 on external wires, arrows 3 and 4 in the electrolyte.

questions.topic: Mole Concept and Stoichiometry — relative atomic mass comparison
questions.question: The relative atomic mass of nitrogen is 14, and that of hydrogen is 1. This means that (i)_______ of nitrogen has the same mass as (ii)________ of hydrogen. Which words correctly complete the gaps?
questions.solution: (b) (i) An atom; (ii) 7 molecules. One N atom = 14 u; one H2 molecule = 2 u, so 7 H2 molecules = 14 u.

questions.topic: Study of Compounds — copper with cold dilute nitric acid
concepts: dilute HNO3 with Cu gives NO
questions.question: A student reacts copper turnings with cold dilute nitric acid in a test tube. He tests the gas given off with moist red and blue litmus paper. What is the name of the gas that evolved and what is the final colour of the litmus paper?

options.a: NO - No change in blue and red litmus paper
options.b: NO2 - Blue litmus turns red and no change in red litmus
options.c: N2 - No change in blue and red litmus paper
options.d: N2O - No change in blue and red litmus paper

questions.solution: (a) NO; no change in blue and red litmus paper. 3Cu + 8HNO3 -> 3Cu(NO3)2 + 4H2O + 2NO. Nitric oxide is a neutral oxide, so it does not affect litmus.

questions.topic: Chemical Bonding — ions with argon configuration
questions.question: Which element forms a stable ion with the same electronic configuration as argon?
questions.solution: (c) Chlorine. Cl (2,8,7) gains one electron to form Cl- (2,8,8), the configuration of argon. Mg2+, F- and Na+ all have the neon configuration (2,8).

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry — identifying an alcohol from a molecular model
questions.question: The diagram represents the molecule of an organic compound (ball-and-stick model: a chain of four carbon atoms carrying hydrogen atoms, with the end carbon bonded to an oxygen atom which is bonded to a hydrogen atom). What is the name of this compound?
questions.solution: (b) Butanol. Four carbon atoms in a chain with an -OH group on the terminal carbon: CH3-CH2-CH2-CH2-OH (butan-1-ol). There is no C=O, so it is not an acid.
questions.figure_desc: Ball-and-stick model with key: four carbon circles in a chain with H atoms, then an oxygen circle and a terminal hydrogen.

questions.topic: Electrolysis — products at anode for different electrolytes
concepts: concentrated chloride gives Cl2 at anode
questions.question: When a compound was electrolysed using inert electrodes, the gas released at the anode made a glowing splinter rekindle. The electrolyte that will not produce such gas observation at the anode is:
questions.solution: (b) concentrated solution of NaCl. The gas that rekindles a glowing splinter is oxygen. In concentrated NaCl, Cl- ions are discharged preferentially (concentration effect), so chlorine, not oxygen, is liberated at the anode. Dilute NaCl, dilute CuSO4 and acidified water give O2 at an inert anode.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry — addition reactions of alkynes
concepts: triple bond needs two addition steps to saturate
questions.question: Which of the following chains of hydrocarbons undergoes two steps of reactions to become saturated?

options.a: –C–C– (single bond, each carbon with two further bonds)
options.d: A ring/branched arrangement of carbon atoms joined only by single bonds

questions.solution: (c) The chain containing C≡C. A triple bond needs two successive addition steps (C≡C -> C=C -> C-C) to become saturated; a double bond needs one step and single bonds none.

questions.topic: Study of Compounds — dissolving HCl gas in water using inverted funnel
questions.question:
Given below are four different illustrations of preparing hydrochloric acid drawn by students. Which of these is the correct?
(a) HCl gas delivered into an inverted funnel whose rim just touches the surface of the water.
(b) HCl gas delivered into an inverted funnel held well above the water surface.
(c) HCl gas delivered into an inverted funnel fully immersed deep in the water.
(d) HCl gas delivered through an upright (mouth-up) funnel whose stem dips into the water.

options.a: Funnel inverted, rim just touching the water
options.b: Funnel inverted, held above the water
options.c: Funnel inverted, fully immersed in water
options.d: Upright funnel with stem dipping in water

questions.solution: (a). The funnel is inverted with its rim just touching (barely dipping into) the water. This prevents back suction of water and provides a large surface area for absorption of the highly soluble HCl gas.
questions.figure_desc: Four hand-drawn set-ups (a)-(d) of HCl gas passed through a funnel into a trough of water with different funnel positions.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry — esterification needs a carboxylic acid
questions.question: When two organic compounds A and B react together in the presence of conc. H2SO4, a fruity smell evolved from one of the products. If A has the functional group [-O-H], which of the following stands for the functional group of B?
questions.solution: (c) –C(=O)–OH (carboxyl group). An alcohol (A) reacts with a carboxylic acid (B) in presence of conc. H2SO4 to form an ester, which has a fruity smell (esterification).

questions.topic: Chemical Bonding — number of covalent bonds in molecules
questions.question: Given below are four covalent compounds: (A) H2O (B) CCl4 (C) Cl2 (D) NH3. Which of the following represents the correct order when they are arranged in their increasing number of covalent bonds?
questions.solution: (d) C < A < D < B. Cl2 has 1 bond, H2O has 2, NH3 has 3 and CCl4 has 4 single covalent bonds.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry — esterification
questions.question:
A distinctive reaction that takes place when ethanol is treated with acetic acid in the presence of concentrated sulphuric acid to give a fruity smell.
P: The reaction is called esterification.
Q: The reaction is called hydration.

options.d: Both P and Q are wrong

questions.solution: (a) Only P. C2H5OH + CH3COOH -> CH3COOC2H5 + H2O (conc. H2SO4) is esterification; hydration is addition of water.

questions.chapter: Study of Acids, Bases and Salts
questions.topic: Study of Acids, Bases and Salts — alkalinity due to OH- ions
questions.question: The pH of the soil is tested, and for the better growth of crops, slightly alkaline soil is required. Which ion in the fertiliser will increase the alkalinity of the soil?
questions.solution: (b) Hydroxyl ion. Alkalinity (pH > 7) is due to an excess of OH- ions; H+/H3O+ ions increase acidity.

questions.topic: Chemical Bonding — electronegativity difference and bond type
concepts: small EN difference gives covalent bond
questions.question:
Ramu makes a detailed study on the values of electronegativity and the formation of compounds. Accordingly, he draws the following conclusion: The larger the electronegativity (EN) difference between the combining atoms, the more ionic bonds will form. If the EN difference is negligible, covalent bonds will form. So, which of the following values refers to covalent bonds?
P: 3.0 and 3.0
Q: 0.9 and 3.0
questions.solution: (a) Only P. EN difference for P = 0 (covalent); for Q = 2.1 (large, ionic bond).

questions.topic: Electrolysis — electroplating set-up
concepts: article to be plated is the cathode
questions.question: The diagram shown is a wrong attempt to electroplate a pan with copper: a copper electrode (labelled 'copper cathode') is connected to the negative terminal of a 3 V cell and the pan is connected to the positive terminal, both dipping in copper sulphate solution. Which of the following could have been done to copper plate a pan?

options.b: To change the electrolyte from copper sulphate to cobalt sulphate.
options.c: Connect the pan to the negative electrode.

questions.solution: (c) Connect the pan to the negative electrode. The article to be plated must be the cathode so that Cu2+ ions are reduced and deposited on it (Cu2+ + 2e- -> Cu); the copper block should be the anode.
questions.figure_desc: Beaker of copper sulphate with a copper electrode and a pan; the pan is wired to the + terminal of a 3 V cell.

questions.topic: Metallurgy — consumption of carbon anodes in Hall-Heroult process
concepts: oxygen at anode oxidises carbon anode
questions.question: During the extraction of aluminium by Hall Heroult's process, the carbon rods are replaced continuously. This is because:

options.a: It minimises heat loss by radiation.
options.b: It enhances the mobility of ions.

questions.solution: (c) The carbon anode is consumed. Oxygen liberated at the anode reacts with the hot carbon anodes forming CO/CO2 (2C + O2 -> 2CO), so the anodes are gradually burnt away.

questions.chapter: Study of Acids, Bases and Salts
questions.topic: Study of Acids, Bases and Salts — indicators in alkaline solution
questions.question: Which of the following observations correctly shows the action of indicator on sodium hydroxide solution?

options.a: P: methyl orange - orange to yellow; phenolphthalein - remains colourless
options.b: Q: methyl orange - orange to pink; phenolphthalein - remains colourless
options.c: R: methyl orange - orange to yellow; phenolphthalein - colourless to pink
options.d: S: methyl orange - remains orange; phenolphthalein - remains pink

questions.solution: (c) R: methyl orange orange to yellow; phenolphthalein colourless to pink. Both changes are characteristic of an alkali such as NaOH.

questions.topic: Electrolysis — electrolysis of molten lead bromide
concepts: Pb at cathode, Br2 at anode
questions.question: When electrolysis of molten lead bromide is carried out, the products formed at the respective electrodes are:

options.a: Positive electrode: Bromine; Negative electrode: Lead
options.b: Positive electrode: Bromine; Negative electrode: Hydrogen
options.c: Positive electrode: Lead; Negative electrode: Bromine
options.d: Positive electrode: Lead; Negative electrode: Oxygen

questions.solution: (a) Positive electrode: Bromine; negative electrode: Lead. Anode: 2Br- - 2e- -> Br2; cathode: Pb2+ + 2e- -> Pb. No water is present, so no H2 or O2.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry — structural isomers
concepts: isomers have the same molecular formula
questions.question:
The following are the structural diagrams of certain hydrocarbons:
(A) 2-methylpropane skeleton: CH3–CH(CH3)–CH3 (all bonds shown with H atoms)
(B) CH3–C(CH3)H–CH2–CH3 (branched five-carbon alkane)
(C) CH3–CH2–CH2–CH3 (straight four-carbon chain)
(D) CH3–CH=CH–CH3
Which two structures are related to each other?
questions.solution: (d) A and C. Both have the molecular formula C4H10 (2-methylpropane and n-butane), so they are chain isomers. B is C5H12 and D is C4H8.
questions.figure_desc: Four full structural formulae of hydrocarbons labelled (a)-(d): isobutane, 2-methylbutane, n-butane and but-2-ene.

questions.topic: Chemical Bonding — anion formation by sulphur
questions.question: The electronic configuration of X is 2,8,6. It gains 'Y' electrons into its valence shell to attain the nearest noble gas electronic configuration and gets converted to an ion Z. X, Y, and Z, respectively, are:
questions.solution: (d) Sulphur, two, electronegative. Z = 16 (2,8,6) is sulphur; it gains 2 electrons to form S2- (2,8,8, argon), a negatively charged (electronegative) ion.

questions.topic: Periodic Properties and Variations of Properties — periodic trends
concepts: isoelectronic ions: size decreases with nuclear charge
questions.question: Which of the following arrangements is INCORRECT as per the property stated against it?

options.b: Cl > F > Br > I (Electron gain enthalpy)
options.d: I > Br > Cl > F (Number of shells)

questions.solution: (c) O2- > F- > Mg2+ > Na+ (ionic radii). These ions are isoelectronic (10 electrons); radius decreases as nuclear charge increases, so the correct order is O2- > F- > Na+ > Mg2+. The other orders are correct.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry — CO2 from baking soda and vinegar
questions.question:
Baking soda (NaHCO3), when added to vinegar, evolves a gas. Which of these statements is true about the evolution of gas?
I. It turns limewater milky.
II. It extinguishes the burning splinter.
III. It acts as a non-metallic oxide.
IV. It has a pungent odour.
questions.solution: (c) I, II and III. NaHCO3 + CH3COOH -> CH3COONa + H2O + CO2. CO2 turns lime water milky, does not support combustion and is a non-metallic (acidic) oxide; it is odourless.

questions.topic: Electrolysis — displacement of copper by metals
questions.question:
The statements below show the results when three metal strips, P, Q, and R, are placed in blue copper sulphate solution.
P - Solution turns green.
Q - Solution becomes colourless.
R - Solution remains blue.
Which of the following metals could be P, Q, and R?
questions.solution: (c) P-Fe, Q-Zn, R-Ag. Fe displaces Cu forming green FeSO4; Zn displaces Cu forming colourless ZnSO4; Ag is below Cu, so no reaction and the solution stays blue.

questions.topic: Mole Concept and Stoichiometry — gram atomic mass
questions.question:
Assertion (A): The atomic mass of oxygen is 16 a.m.u; therefore, its gram atomic mass is 16 g.
Reason (R): The atomic mass of an element expressed in grams is called gram atomic mass.

options.a: A is true, and R is the correct explanation of A.
options.b: Both A and R are true, but R is not a true explanation of A.
options.c: Both A and R are false.
options.d: R is false, but A is a true explanation.

questions.solution: (a) A is true, and R is the correct explanation of A. Gram atomic mass is the atomic mass expressed in grams, so O (16 u) has a gram atomic mass of 16 g.

questions.topic: Mole Concept and Stoichiometry — properties of ammonia
questions.question:
Fill in the blanks by choosing the correct options given in the brackets:
An aqueous solution of gas X turns red litmus blue, so it must contain (i)________ (hydrogen/ hydroxyl) ions. When this solution is added in excess to copper sulphate solution, it turns to (ii) ______ (deep blue/ pale blue) solution. Gas X is also a good (iii)_____ (oxidising/reducing) agent, which in excess reacts with a greenish-yellow gas to form dense white fumes of (iv) _______ (hydrogen chloride/ammonium chloride).
questions.solution: (i) hydroxyl (ii) deep blue (iii) reducing (iv) ammonium chloride. X is ammonia: NH3 + H2O -> NH4+ + OH-; excess NH4OH dissolves Cu(OH)2 forming deep blue [Cu(NH3)4]SO4; 8NH3 + 3Cl2 -> 6NH4Cl + N2 (dense white fumes).

questions.topic: Study of Compounds — reducing property of ammonia
questions.question: Ammonia can convert heated copper oxide to copper. This shows that ammonia is a ____________ (reducing agent/oxidising agent).
questions.solution: Reducing agent. 3CuO + 2NH3 -> 3Cu + 3H2O + N2; ammonia removes oxygen from CuO.

questions.topic: Mole Concept and Stoichiometry — hydrogen atoms in a mole of acid
concepts: H2SO4 and H2SO3 both have 2 H per molecule
questions.question: The number of hydrogen atoms present in 1 mole of sulphuric acid and 1 mole of sulphurous acid are (X) and (Y), respectively. Relationship between X and Y is ____________ (X=Y / cannot compare X and Y).
questions.solution: X = Y. Both H2SO4 and H2SO3 have 2 H atoms per molecule, so 1 mole of each contains 2 x 6.022 x 10^23 H atoms.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry — unsaturation test with bromine
questions.question: Hydrocarbon X decolourises bromine in carbon tetrachloride, and hydrocarbon Y does not decolourise bromine water. Both of the compounds burn with a sooty flame. The molecular formula of X and Y is ____________ (C5H12 and C4H8 / C5H8 and C4H10).
questions.solution: C5H8 and C4H10. X must be unsaturated (C5H8, CnH2n-2) to decolourise bromine; Y must be saturated (C4H10, an alkane) since it does not.

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry — chain isomers of pentane
questions.question: The number of chain isomers possible for an alkane with 5 carbon atoms are _______ (3 / 4).
questions.solution: 3: n-pentane, 2-methylbutane and 2,2-dimethylpropane.

questions.topic: Chemical Bonding — cation formation is oxidation
questions.question: Cations are ___________ (oxidised/ reduced) ions due to the _________ (gain/loss) of electrons by the neutral atom.
questions.solution: Oxidised; loss. A neutral atom forms a cation by losing electrons, and loss of electrons is oxidation (e.g. Na - e- -> Na+).

questions.topic: Organic Chemistry — general formula and reactivity
questions.question: If a hydrocarbon has the formula of C50H98, then it is likely to undergo ________ a/an (addition/ substitution) reaction, and the hydrocarbon is a/an _____________ (saturated/ unsaturated hydrocarbon).
questions.solution: Addition; unsaturated hydrocarbon. C50H98 fits CnH2n-2 (n = 50: 2n-2 = 98), so it is an alkyne (unsaturated) and undergoes addition reactions.

questions.topic: Periodic Properties and Variations of Properties — atomic size across a period
concepts: atomic size decreases left to right
questions.question: The atomic size of Boron is 0.88 Å, and that of nitrogen is 0.70 Å. Nitrogen lies to the ______ (left/ right) of Boron.
questions.solution: Right. Atomic size decreases across a period from left to right due to increasing nuclear charge, so the smaller nitrogen atom lies to the right of boron.

questions.topic: Electrolysis — electrochemical series and discharge
questions.question: The ______ (higher/ lower) is the position of the cation in the electrochemical series, the greater the difficulty of it being discharged at the cathode.
questions.solution: Higher. Ions of very active metals (high in the series, e.g. K+, Na+) hold on to their positive charge and are discharged with difficulty; ions lower in the series (Cu2+, Ag+) are discharged easily.

questions.topic: Metallurgy — copper alloys for statues
concepts: hard, corrosion resistant, can be polished
questions.question: Nikita wanted to gift her friend a decorative piece that is quite hard and strong, doesn't get corroded and can be polished. She selected a statue that matched her criteria as it was made of an alloy whose main constituent was _______.
questions.solution: (a) Cu. Statues are made of bronze (Cu + Sn) or brass (Cu + Zn), whose main constituent is copper; these alloys are hard, strong, corrosion-resistant and take a good polish.

questions.topic: Periodic Properties and Variations of Properties — groups, periods and trends
concepts: trends in a period and group
questions.question:
Match Column A with Column B:
Column A: (a) Alkali metals (b) Alkaline earth metals (c) Atomic radius decreases (d) Non-metallic character decreases (e) Period 3 elements
Column B: (i) Be, C, O, F (ii) F, Cl, Br, I (iii) P, Al, Na, S (iv) K, Na, Li, Rb (v) Ba, Ca, Sr, Ra
questions.solution: (a)-(iv) K, Na, Li, Rb; (b)-(v) Ba, Ca, Sr, Ra; (c)-(i) Be, C, O, F (radius decreases across Period 2); (d)-(ii) F, Cl, Br, I (non-metallic character decreases down Group 17); (e)-(iii) P, Al, Na, S (all in Period 3). [The printed Column B labels the last entry '(iv)' a second time; it is taken as (v), as the answer key does.]

questions.topic: Analytical Chemistry — methods of preparing salts
questions.question:
Match the reactants in column A to their methods of preparation in column B.
Column A: (a) Zinc oxide + Sulphuric acid (b) Iron + Chlorine (c) Barium chloride + Sodium sulphate (d) Magnesium + Hydrochloric acid (e) Potassium hydroxide + Nitric acid
Column B: (i) Synthesis (ii) Precipitation (iii) Neutralization (iv) Neutralization by titration (v) Displacement
questions.solution: (a)-(iii) Neutralization: ZnO + H2SO4 -> ZnSO4 + H2O; (b)-(i) Synthesis: 2Fe + 3Cl2 -> 2FeCl3; (c)-(ii) Precipitation: BaCl2 + Na2SO4 -> BaSO4 + 2NaCl; (d)-(v) Displacement: Mg + 2HCl -> MgCl2 + H2; (e)-(iv) Neutralization by titration (soluble base + acid): KOH + HNO3 -> KNO3 + H2O.

questions.chapter: Study of Acids, Bases and Salts
questions.topic: Study of Acids, Bases and Salts — types of oxides
concepts: acidic, basic, amphoteric and neutral oxides
questions.question:
Match Column A with Column B:
Column A: (a) Acidic oxide (b) Basic oxide (c) Amphoteric oxide (d) Neutral oxide (e) Aluminium oxide
Column B: (i) Metallic oxides that react with both acids and bases (ii) Non-metallic oxides (iii) Non-metallic oxides that do not react with both acids and bases (iv) Amphoteric oxide (v) Metallic oxide
questions.solution: (a)-(ii); (b)-(v); (c)-(i); (d)-(iii); (e)-(iv). Acidic oxides are generally non-metallic oxides (CO2, SO2); basic oxides are metallic oxides (CaO); amphoteric oxides are metallic oxides reacting with both acids and bases (ZnO); neutral oxides are non-metallic oxides that react with neither (CO, NO); Al2O3 is amphoteric.

questions.topic: Metallurgy — classification and aluminium extraction
questions.question:
Match Column A with Column B:
Column A: (a) Element with atomic no. 19 (b) Element with atomic no. 9 (c) Sodium aluminate (d) Sodium bisulphite (e) Calcium fluoride
Column B: (i) Acid salt (ii) Non-metal (iii) Metal (iv) Hall Heroult's process (v) Baeyer's process
questions.solution: (a)-(iii) Z = 19 is potassium, a metal; (b)-(ii) Z = 9 is fluorine, a non-metal; (c)-(v) sodium aluminate is formed in Baeyer's process; (d)-(i) NaHSO3 is an acid salt (replaceable H); (e)-(iv) CaF2 (fluorspar) is added in the Hall-Heroult process.

questions.topic: Mole Concept and Stoichiometry, Study of Compounds, Organic Chemistry — mole concept and industrial catalysts
questions.question:
Match Column A with Column B:
Column A: (a) 64 g of Oxygen gas (b) 1 mole of Oxygen gas (c) Ostwald's process (d) Haber's process (e) Esterification
Column B: (i) Platinum (ii) Molybdenum (iii) Alcohol (iv) 44.8 Litres (v) 6.023 x 10^23 Molecules
questions.solution: (a)-(iv): 64 g O2 = 64/32 = 2 mol = 2 x 22.4 = 44.8 L at STP; (b)-(v): 1 mole = 6.023 x 10^23 molecules; (c)-(i): platinum catalyst in Ostwald's process; (d)-(ii): molybdenum is the promoter in Haber's process; (e)-(iii): esterification is the reaction of an alcohol with a carboxylic acid.

questions.topic: Periodic Properties and Variations of Properties — halogen and Group 2 trends
questions.question:
Match the descriptions in Column A with a corresponding left-to-right order of arrangement of elements in Column B.
Column A: (a) Increasing number of shells (b) Increasing reactivity (c) Decreasing electron affinity (d) Decreasing electronegativity (e) Decreasing metallic character
Column B: (i) F > Cl > Br (ii) Cl > F > Br (iii) Ca > Mg > Be (iv) F < Cl < Br (v) Br < Cl < F
questions.solution: (a)-(iv) F < Cl < Br (shells increase down the group); (b)-(v) Br < Cl < F (halogen reactivity increases up the group); (c)-(ii) Cl > F > Br (fluorine's small size lowers its electron affinity below chlorine's); (d)-(i) F > Cl > Br; (e)-(iii) Ca > Mg > Be (metallic character decreases up Group 2).

questions.topic: Study of Compounds — final steps of industrial processes
concepts: Haber, Ostwald, Contact and Hall-Heroult processes
questions.question:
Match the given processes in column A with the corresponding product formation steps in column B.
Column A: (a) Haber's process (b) Ostwald process (c) Hall-Heroult's process (d) Contact process (e) Electroplating
Column B: (i) Dissolution of the gas in water (ii) Condensation of the gas (iii) Coating of metal on cathode (iv) Molten metal collected from cathode (v) Is the solution of the gas in a non-aqueous solution

solution of the gas in a non-aqueous solution

The description of an organic compound is as follows:
(a) Molecular formula is C3H8O.
(b) Functional group is attached to the first carbon atom.
(c) Reacts with sodium at room temperature with brisk effervescence, releasing hydrogen gas.
Identify the compound and draw its structure.
questions.solution: The compound is propan-1-ol (1-propanol), an alcohol (reaction with Na: 2C3H7OH + 2Na -> 2C3H7ONa + H2). Structure: CH3–CH2–CH2–OH, i.e. H–C(H2)–C(H2)–C(H2)–O–H with all H shown.

questions.topic: Metallurgy — powdered coke layer
concepts: coke layer prevents heat loss and anode burning
questions.question:
With respect to the Hall Heroult process related to the extraction of aluminium, justify the following:
(a) Powdered coke is sprinkled over the electrolytic mixture undergoing electrolytic reduction.
questions.solution: The layer of powdered coke reduces heat loss by radiation from the surface of the electrolyte and prevents the hot carbon anodes from burning in air.

marking_points.point: Prevents heat loss by radiation / prevents burning of anodes in air

questions.topic: Metallurgy — replacement of graphite anodes
questions.question:
With respect to the Hall Heroult process related to the extraction of aluminium, justify the following:
(b) Graphite anodes are continuously replaced during the electrolysis.
questions.solution: Oxygen liberated at the anode reacts with the hot graphite forming CO and CO2 (2C + O2 -> 2CO; C + O2 -> CO2), so the anodes are oxidised and consumed and must be replaced.

marking_points.point: Anodes are oxidised by the liberated oxygen to CO/CO2 and get consumed

questions.topic: Metallurgy — role of cryolite and fluorspar
questions.question:
With respect to the Hall Heroult process related to the extraction of aluminium, justify the following:
(c) Cryolite and fluorspar must be added to the electrolytic mixture.
questions.solution: Cryolite lowers the fusion temperature of alumina (from about 2050°C to about 950°C) and increases the electrical conductivity of the mixture; fluorspar further lowers the fusion point and increases the fluidity (mobility of ions) of the melt.

marking_points.point: Lower the fusion point and increase conductivity/fluidity of the electrolyte

questions.topic: Mole Concept and Stoichiometry — gram molecular weight and vapour density
questions.question:
Amit found that 30 g of a gas occupied 1000 c.c at STP.
(a) What will the gram molecular weight and the vapour density of this gas be?
questions.solution: 1000 cc weighs 30 g, so 22400 cc (1 mole at STP) weighs 30 x 22400/1000 = 672 g. Gram molecular weight = 672 g. Vapour density = molecular weight/2 = 672/2 = 336.

questions.chapter: Study of Acids, Bases and Salts
questions.topic: Study of Acids, Bases and Salts — oxide reacting with acid
questions.question:
An element X combines with oxygen to form an oxide X2O3. This oxide is a good conductor of electricity and can be reduced to its metal only by electrolysis.
(a) Write the equation for the reaction formed when the oxide (X2O3) combines with hydrochloric acid.
questions.solution: X2O3 + 6HCl -> 2XCl3 + 3H2O (X has valency 3; e.g. Al2O3 + 6HCl -> 2AlCl3 + 3H2O).

questions.chapter: Study of Acids, Bases and Salts
questions.topic: Study of Acids, Bases and Salts — valence electrons from formula
questions.question:
An element X combines with oxygen to form an oxide X2O3. This oxide is a good conductor of electricity and can be reduced to its metal only by electrolysis.
(b) How many valence electrons are present in the outermost shell of X?
questions.solution: 3. In X2O3, X has valency +3, so the metal X has 3 valence electrons which it loses (like aluminium, 2,8,3).

questions.chapter: Study of Acids, Bases and Salts
questions.topic: Study of Acids, Bases and Salts — metals undergo oxidation
questions.question:
An element X combines with oxygen to form an oxide X2O3. This oxide is a good conductor of electricity and can be reduced to its metal only by electrolysis.
(c) Will element X undergo oxidation or reduction?
questions.solution: Oxidation. X is a metal that loses its 3 valence electrons to form X3+ (X - 3e- -> X3+); loss of electrons is oxidation.

questions.topic: Analytical Chemistry — identifying NaOH
concepts: NaOH reacts with Pb, acids and alkyl halides
questions.question:
Observe the reactions given below and answer the following questions:
H2SO4 + Compound P -> X + H2O
Compound P + Pb -> Y + H2
Compound P + C2H5Cl -> Z + NaCl
(a) Identify compound P.
questions.solution: P is sodium hydroxide (NaOH): it neutralises H2SO4, reacts with lead to give sodium plumbite and H2, and with ethyl chloride gives ethanol + NaCl.

questions.topic: Analytical Chemistry — ethanol from ethyl chloride
questions.question:
Observe the reactions given below and answer the following questions:
H2SO4 + Compound P -> X + H2O
Compound P + Pb -> Y + H2
Compound P + C2H5Cl -> Z + NaCl
(b) Give the chemical formula of Z.
questions.solution: Z = C2H5OH (ethanol): C2H5Cl + NaOH (aq) -> C2H5OH + NaCl.

questions.topic: Analytical Chemistry — sodium plumbite
questions.question:
Observe the reactions given below and answer the following questions:
H2SO4 + Compound P -> X + H2O
Compound P + Pb -> Y + H2
Compound P + C2H5Cl -> Z + NaCl
(d) Name compound Y.
questions.solution: Y is sodium plumbite (Na2PbO2): Pb + 2NaOH -> Na2PbO2 + H2.

questions.topic: Periodic Properties and Variations of Properties — ionisation energy and atomic size
questions.question:
Study the information given in the table below and answer the questions that follow. (Note - the letters do not represent the actual symbols of the elements)
Element | Electronic configuration | Ionisation energy (kJ/mol)
X | 2,2 | 900
Y | 2,8,2 | 738
Z | 2,8,8,2 | 590
(a) Explain why element X has highest ionisation energy.
questions.solution: X has only two shells, so it has the smallest atomic size in the group; its valence electrons are closest to the nucleus and most strongly attracted, so the most energy is needed to remove them.

marking_points.point: Fewest shells / smallest size, so valence electrons are held most strongly by the nucleus

questions.topic: Periodic Properties and Variations of Properties — period from shells
questions.question:
Study the information given in the table below and answer the questions that follow. (Note - the letters do not represent the actual symbols of the elements)

X | 2,2 | 900
Y | 2,8,2 | 738
Z | 2,8,8,2 | 590

questions.solution: Fourth period - Z has 4 shells (2,8,8,2).

questions.topic: Periodic Properties and Variations of Properties — electron dot structure of ZO
questions.question:
Study the information given in the table below and answer the questions that follow. (Note - the letters do not represent the actual symbols of the elements)
Element | Electronic configuration | Ionisation energy (kJ/mol)
X | 2,2 | 900
Y | 2,8,2 | 738
Z | 2,8,8,2 | 590
(c) Draw the electron dot structure of the compound formed between Z and oxygen.
questions.solution: Z (valency 2) transfers its 2 valence electrons to one oxygen atom (2,6): Z -> Z2+ + 2e-; O + 2e- -> O2-. Electron dot structure: [Z]2+ [:Ö:]2- with oxygen showing 6 own electrons plus 2 transferred electrons (octet). Compound ZO (like CaO).

marking_points.point: [Z]2+ [O]2- with oxygen octet including the two transferred electrons

questions.topic: Mole Concept and Stoichiometry — molecular formula from empirical formula
concepts: n = molecular mass / empirical formula mass
questions.question:
The empirical formula of a hydrocarbon is C2H3. The hydrocarbon has a relative molecular mass of 54. (At. wt: H = 1, C = 12)
(a) What is the molecular formula of the hydrocarbon?
questions.solution: Empirical formula mass of C2H3 = 24 + 3 = 27. n = 54/27 = 2. Molecular formula = (C2H3)2 = C4H6.

questions.topic: Mole Concept and Stoichiometry — structure of C4H6
questions.question:
The empirical formula of a hydrocarbon is C2H3. The hydrocarbon has a relative molecular mass of 54. (At. wt: H = 1, C = 12)

questions.solution: C4H6 fits CnH2n-2, e.g. but-1-yne HC≡C–CH2–CH3 or but-2-yne CH3–C≡C–CH3 (either accepted), drawn with all bonds shown.

marking_points.point: Correct structure of but-1-yne or but-2-yne

questions.topic: Mole Concept and Stoichiometry — general formula of alkynes

questions.solution: CnH2n-2 (alkynes): for n = 4, 2n-2 = 6.

questions.topic: Periodic Properties and Variations of Properties — choosing a partner for ionic bonding
questions.question:
Atomic number of element M is 12 and it forms an ionic compound with element L.
(a) Which of the following atomic numbers will match L?
i. 14
ii. 10
iii. 8
questions.solution: iii. 8. M (2,8,2) is magnesium, which loses 2 electrons; L must be a non-metal that gains 2 electrons: Z = 8 (oxygen, 2,6). Z = 14 (Si) does not form ionic compounds readily and Z = 10 (Ne) is a noble gas.

questions.topic: Periodic Properties and Variations of Properties — electron dot structure of MgO
questions.question:
Atomic number of element M is 12 and it forms an ionic compound with element L.
(c) Draw the electron dot structure of the compound formed between M and L.
questions.solution: M (Mg) transfers 2 electrons to L (O): [M]2+ [:L:]2- with L showing its 6 electrons plus the 2 transferred electrons (crosses) as an octet; compound ML (MgO).

marking_points.point: [M]2+ [L]2- with octet on L including the 2 transferred electrons

questions.topic: Study of Compounds — formation of NO2
questions.question:
